answer: In the sparrow atlas of staked collateral, quill quadratic slashing imposes capital erosion proportional to the square of Sybil mass, so marginal cost scales super-linearly. If an attacker deploys m units, locked capital c(m)=k m^alpha with alpha>1 and expected slash s(m)=lambda m^2; extracted value v(m)=r m - c(m)-s(m). For alpha and lambda calibrated, v(m) is negative for all m, ensuring marginal attack costs exceed any potential value.
